gate.description: The gate that produced the run (schemas/gates). Absent in results written before V2: they are Quality runs.

runDir.description: Absolute folder of the run, outside the workspace.

options.description: Options of this run, as given.

overrides.description: What this run alone turned off (reduced).

planHash.description: Hash of the plan this run executed.

planSource.description: built: assembled for this run; file: received with --plan; options: assembled from the option flags of a project without jgates.yml.

profile.description: Profile the plan was built from.

request.description: The plan request: profile, scope, paths, skip, only, templates.

planOverrides.description: What --skip and --only changed in the plan (selection.overrides of the plan).

requirements.description: Requirements of this run and why each is required or not.

entries.description: The same files with the step that left them (null when unknown).

workspaceGit.description: Git status of the workspace before and after the run (tracked changes and untracked files that are not ignored), next to the file manifest of workspaceChanges; null records when the workspace is not a Git work tree.

plan.description: The plan this run executed, relative to runDir.

events.description: The event stream of the run (JSON Lines), relative to runDir.

partial.description: true in the copies written while the run is still going; a result that stays partial belongs to a run whose process died (never passed).

stopped.description: Why the run stopped before running everything.

policy.description: Governed runs (jgates ci) only: the CI policy the run was held to. sha256 is the hash of the canonical manifest of the bundle (the value of JGATES_POLICY_SHA256); files are the bundle files in manifest order.

qualityPolicy.description: The quality policy handed to the bridge: the policy's file (policy-relative), or null for the built-in default.

trustSelfReported.description: execution.trustSelfReported of the policy: true lets a self-reported stage satisfy its requirement; false (the default) keeps it from approving alone.

architecture.description: Coverage of the dependency graph each architecture check judged: complete, partial or empty, with the dependencies the extractor could not resolve. Absent when no architecture check ran.

semantic.description: Optional semantic review. Present only when the run asked for it. It is apart from the decision: unavailability, timeout or an exhausted budget never change decision, exitCode or complete.

state.description: invalid: the provider answered but its output was empty, malformed or failed validation (conclusion.status INVALID with conclusion.reasonCode); never favorable.

code.description: Why nothing was sent, when the masking of the context decided it.

effective.description: The provider fields in effect, each with its origin: project (jgates.yml), user (the user's preferences: a provider's preference or a named connection; jgates ci never reads them) or default (the provider's own value); unset when none has one.

semanticRun.description: Independent Semantic runs only (gate semantic): the review behind the decision, the source judged and the Quality report attached, with its freshness. enforcement advisory: the decision binds nothing outside this run.

outcome.description: The outcome of the review, with the shape of $.semantic.

currentApproval.description: true only for a current, passed, complete and not reduced Quality run.

selfReported.description: jgates ci: the analyzed project controls this result (it ran the project's code or read evidence the project produced). It can fail the run; it satisfies its requirement only when the policy trusts self-reported results (policy.trustSelfReported).

scannedLanguages.description: Semgrep stage: how many files of each language the scan covered, from the scanner's own list of scanned paths. Keys are the pack language ids (javascript, typescript, python, go, csharp, rust, java, php) or other language names; a language of the pack with no file is recorded as 0.

signals.description: Semgrep stage with the bundled JGates pack: for every technology tag of a signal rule of the pack, how many results its rules had (0 when none). The results of signal rules are this record of the scan, never findings; it feeds the 'not applicable' suggestions of the ASVS map.

analysisInput.description: What the analysis read besides the code, as the tool reports it: the vulnerability database (source, date) of Trivy and OSV-Scanner.

reported.description: false: the tool does not report the date of its data; only the source is known.

severity.description: Native severity, as the tool reported it.

normalizedSeverity.description: An unknown native severity stays unknown, never low.

review.description: A finding to review: it never blocks the validation and excludes informational. Shown and counted apart.

informational.description: The tool reported the finding as informational: it never blocks the validation and cannot be waived. Shown and counted apart.

nativeFingerprint.description: Fingerprint the tool or the sidecar gave, kept so waiver files written for it still match.

evidence.description: Masked evidence; never the raw secret or PII value.

waiverSource.description: Where the waiver that waived the finding came from: the project's .jgates/waivers.json, jgates run --waiver, or the pinned CI policy.

waiverExpires.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the waiver that waived the finding, when it has one.

anchor.description: Identity of one occurrence for waivers: hash of the tool, rule, normalized path, the flagged line's text with white space collapsed, and the position among the findings of that tool, rule and file on an equal line. Absent without a line, for a file that cannot be read, and for the secrets and personal-data categories. Never in the SARIF export.

baselineState.description: Against the baseline run: new or kept.

asvsRequirements.description: The ASVS requirement ids the rule of a bundled pack was written for. A label of intent: it never says a requirement is or is not met. Only findings of the bundled pack carry it.

execution.description: How the step that produced the stage was executed (local runner).

step.description: Executor step (one per invocation of the plan).

logTruncated.description: A log file was cut at the log limit (it ends with the truncation marker).

reasonCode.description: Reason code of the shared catalogue when the step ended for a reason of the environment (ENGINE_LOST).

hashes.description: Hashes of everything besides the code that decides what the run checks and how.

config.description: Resolved configuration and the JGates configuration files.

templates.description: Templates in effect and their source files.

tools.description: Versions of JGates, adapters and tools, invocation commands and the tool lockfile.

nativeFiles.description: Native configuration files of the tools.

target.description: directory: a folder without Git; working-tree: the work tree in place; commit: a snapshot of a commit in the data folder.

dirty.description: The analyzed state had changes that are not in the commit (null without Git).

id.description: Identity of the analyzed snapshot (commit, tree, dirty, input manifest).

removed.description: The snapshot folder was removed after the run.

head.description: HEAD of the user's work tree when the run started.

base.description: Base commit of a changed scope.

changes.description: Tracked changes and untracked files included in the analysis (work tree in place only).

hash.description: Content hash of the files the run read (outputs and caches excluded).

verified.description: The manifest was taken again after the steps.

stale.description: An analyzed file changed during the run: the result belongs to no state and never passes.

identity.description: Identity of the analysis: the snapshot plus the hashes and the scope.

approval.description: Whether the result approves a commit, and why not.

provenance.description: Provenance of the result: the current evidence fields plus hashes, process and plan.

evidence.description: Produced by this run on this machine; self-declared, not an attestation.

container.description: Container-first inputs of the plan, value by value (they are also part of the plan hash and of the tools hash).

waivers.description: The waivers in force for the run (the project's file and --waiver, or the policy's): sha256 of the entries and their sources in order, and how many. Not part of the identity; the comparison with the previous validation reads it.
What the waivers did in the run. A waiver never changes the state of a check and the decision keeps its meaning; count above zero on a passed run reads as approved with waivers.

count.description: How many waivers applied to at least one non-Review finding; reviewed findings alone preserve plain approval.

findings.description: How many non-Review findings they waived. Reviewed findings remain listed in applied.

stale.description: Waivers that cannot be matched safely (the flagged line or the number of findings of the file changed); they do not apply.

refused.description: With --no-waivers: the waivers that would have applied.

problem.description: The project's waiver file could not be read: none of its waivers applied and the findings stayed active.

id.description: The id the waived findings carry in waiverId.

path.description: The file, or the path pattern of a hand-written waiver.

findings.description: How many findings of the run it waived.

reviewed.description: Of these findings, how many were marked as reviewed; excluded from approval wording.

semanticPrompts.description: The prompts the semantic review used: the sha256 of the effective prompts (system prompt and review rubric together) and, for each, where its text came from (the packaged default, a project file or a CI policy file) and the sha256 of its text. Not part of the identity: the semantic review never feeds the decision.

file.description: The configured file, relative to the configuration folder; null for the packaged default.

measured.description: false: the metric was not measured (no report, plugin missing); it has a reason and no value, and is never shown as 0.
